Summary  
Data source overview: The paper proposes a decentralized “AI marketplace” to democratise access to AI models and data. It surveys technical, economic and regulatory barriers—privacy, market dominance, information asymmetry, malicious behaviour, and compliance—and describes mechanisms (federated learning, differential privacy, blockchain audit logs, interoperability standards, third-party evaluation, automated regulatory checks) that could overcome them.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]  
The fabric maps every articulated risk through problem analyses, insights, design rationales, mechanisms, evidence and five actionable interventions. I am moderately confident (83 / 100) that the JSON is syntactically correct, nodes are merge-able, paths are interconnected and edge directions follow the required template.  

Instruction-set improvement:  
1. Ask explicitly for the shortest unique “section title or paragraph anchor” rather than “closest preceding section title”; many papers (like this) use sub-sub-sections without clear titles, forcing heuristic choices.  
2. Provide a fixed list of acceptable edge verbs with definitions to reduce synonym drift across 500 k extractions.  
3. Clarify how to treat interventions that are architectural (Model Design) but span multiple lifecycles.  

Inference strategy justification:  
Light inference (edge confidence = 2) was used only where the paper implies but does not empirically prove a link (e.g., decentralisation reduces dominance). All interventions come directly from mechanisms the paper proposes.  

Extraction completeness explanation:  
All five major risk themes discussed are included. Each theme is mapped through every required node category to at least one intervention, and shared implementation/evidence nodes inter-connect the fabric, eliminating isolates. Node count (30) aligns with guideline (~15/5 k words, source ≈10 k words).  

Key limitations:  
• Validation evidence is sometimes indirect literature citations, not primary experiments.  
• Interventions are high-level prototypes (maturity ≤ 2).  
• Some regulatory aspects were condensed; future updates may refine them as standards crystallise.
